lesson.title: Containers from Zero, part 6: Compose for that pair
lesson.description: Replace the network, the volume and both docker run commands from part 5 with one compose.yaml. Start, inspect, change and stop the pair with docker compose, and see what it creates and what down removes.
lesson.tested: Ran the web and proxy pair from one compose.yaml with Compose v5.8.0 on Engine 29.10.1, 25 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Write the pair down once in compose.yaml, start it with docker compose up -d, and remember that down -v deletes the data.

cheatsheet.intro: compose.yaml keys, the names Compose gives things, and what up and down do, from Lesson 6.

boards.title: From docker run to compose.yaml
boards.hint: docker compose, with a space; Compose v5.8.0

rows.name: name:
rows.role: The project name; otherwise the folder name.

rows.name: build: .
rows.role: `docker build .`; the image is named project-service.

rows.name: image:
rows.role: The image at the end of `docker run`.

rows.name: volumes: (service)
rows.role: `--mount`: a volume name, or a path relative to compose.yaml.

rows.name: depends_on:
rows.role: Starting things in order by hand. Waits for running, not ready.

rows.name: (no line)
rows.where: `hello_default`; services find each other by name

boards.title: What each command does
boards.hint: run in the folder with compose.yaml

rows.name: up -d
rows.role: Builds and creates what is missing, starts it in order. Later runs recreate only changed services.

rows.name: down
rows.role: Stops (reverse order) and removes containers and the default network.

rows.name: down -v
rows.role: Also removes named volumes and anonymous volumes of the containers.

rows.name: restart proxy
rows.role: Restarts one service's container. nginx looks `web` up again.

boards.note: `up` does not rebuild an existing image: use `docker compose up -d --build` after changing `app.py`.

steps.title: What the lab showed
steps.hint: IDs, addresses and times differ on your machine

items.what: Printed the full model: `type: bind`, `host_ip: 127.0.0.1`, `condition: service_started`, `hello_default`, `hello_hello-data`.
Built `hello-web`, created network and volume, started `web` then `proxy`. The first `curl`: `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`; then visit 1, visit 2.
A new `web` container carried on at visit 3.
`GREETING: Shalom`: `hello-proxy-1 Running`, `hello-web-1 Recreated`, `Shalom from container ..., visit 4`.
`web` moved to `172.18.0.4`; nginx still tried `upstream: "http://172.18.0.2:8000/"` and answered 502 until `docker compose restart proxy`.

steps.note: Safety: the lab publishes 127.0.0.1:8080. `docker compose down -v` deletes the volume `hello_hello-data` and the count. Change `name: hello` if you already have a project called hello. Undo with `docker compose down -v` in the `hello` folder.

homework.intro: Use the hello folder, compose.yaml and proxy.conf from the lesson. IDs, addresses and times will differ. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What is the difference between `docker compose` and `docker-compose`?
exercises.a: `docker compose`, with a space, is the current Compose, v2 or v5. `docker-compose`, with a hyphen, was Compose v1, written in Python.

exercises.q: Which network do the services join when `compose.yaml` has no `networks:` key, and how do they find each other?
exercises.a: A network named `<project-name>_default`, here `hello_default`. Each service registers its name with Docker's DNS, so `web` resolves.

exercises.q: What does `depends_on: [web]` guarantee, and what does it not?
exercises.a: Compose starts `web` before `proxy`. It waits only until the container is running, not until the program inside is ready.

exercises.q: What does `docker compose up -d` do when you run it again after editing the file?
exercises.a: It recreates only the services whose configuration changed, preserving mounted volumes, and leaves the others running.

exercises.q: What does `docker compose down` keep, and what does `-v` add?
exercises.a: `down` removes containers and the default network, and keeps named volumes and images. `-v` also removes the named volumes and anonymous volumes.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose config`. What does it show for the proxy's port and for `depends_on`?
exercises.a: The port as `host_ip: 127.0.0.1`, `target: 80`, `published: "8080"`. `depends_on` as `condition: service_started`, which means running.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose up -d` and `curl` at once. What can the first request return, and why?
exercises.a: `Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` or `502 Bad Gateway`. The containers were started, but nginx or the app was not listening yet.

exercises.q: Run `docker compose down`, then `up -d`, then `curl`. What count do you get?
exercises.a: The count continues, visit 3 in the lesson, from a new `web` container. `down` kept the volume `hello_hello-data`.

exercises.q: Change `GREETING` and run `docker compose up -d`. Which containers does Compose touch?
List the names Compose gave the containers, the network and the volume. What pattern do you see?
exercises.a: `hello-web-1`, `hello-proxy-1`, `hello_default`, `hello_hello-data`: the project name, then the service or key, and a number for containers.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You change `app.py` and run `docker compose up -d`. Does the change show up?
exercises.a: No. `up` uses the existing image. Run `docker compose up -d --build` to rebuild it.

exercises.q: You indent a line with a tab and run `docker compose config`. What happens?
exercises.a: An error such as `yaml: line 3: found character that cannot start any token`. YAML indentation must use spaces.

exercises.q: You run `docker compose down -v` and then `up -d`. What count does `curl` show, and why?
exercises.a: visit 1. `-v` deleted the volume `hello_hello-data`, so Compose created a new, empty one.

exercises.q: `web` is recreated and gets a new address, and the proxy now answers 502. What happened, and what fixes it?
exercises.a: nginx looked up `web` when it started and kept the old address. `docker compose restart proxy` makes it look the name up again.
